question: What must be true before starting the Hydraulic Power Unit?
expected_answer: Before starting the Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU), four startup interlock conditions must be satisfied: 1) Hydraulic fluid level must be within the normal band on the sight glass; 2) Isolation valve IV-21 must be OPEN; 3) The emergency stop circuit must be RESET; 4) The maintenance access panel must NOT be removed (must be CLOSED).
required_supporting_facts: Fluid level must be within normal band on sight glass
Isolation valve IV-21 must be OPEN
Emergency stop circuit must be RESET
Maintenance access panel must be CLOSED / not removed
applicable_location: operator_manual.pdf: Section 4.3 (Starting the HPU); configuration_export.json: startup_interlocks; screen_01_home.png: HOME screen interlocks
notes: Corroborated across 3 distinct sources (Tier 1 config, Tier 2 manual, Tier 3 HMI screen).

question: What is the current normal operating pressure for the HPU, and under what conditions does that apply?
expected_answer: The current normal operating pressure for the Hydraulic Power Unit is 200 bar. This setpoint applies specifically to units running software revision 3.2 or later equipped with pressure sensor PS-04A (manufactured after 2024). Units running software revisions 3.0 to 3.1 retain the historical 180 bar setpoint.
required_supporting_facts: Normal operating pressure setpoint is 200 bar
Applies to software revision 3.2 and later
Applies to units equipped with sensor PS-04A
applicable_location: ECN-1042.pdf: Section 1; operator_manual.pdf: Section 5; configuration_export.json: revision_applicability
notes: Revised from 180 bar to 200 bar per ECN-1042; distinct from informal 175 bar field note.

question: What does alarm A17 indicate, and what are its possible causes?
expected_answer: Alarm A17 indicates 'Hydraulic Pressure Low', which triggers when discharge line pressure drops below 150 bar (evaluated against whichever sensor is active: PS-04 on SW < 3.2, PS-04A on SW >= 3.2). Its possible causes are: 1) Isolation valve IV-21 closed or partially closed; 2) Low hydraulic fluid level; 3) Pressure sensor signal invalid / sensor drift.
required_supporting_facts: A17 indicates low hydraulic pressure below 150 bar
Possible cause: IV-21 closed or partially closed
Possible cause: low hydraulic fluid level
Possible cause: pressure sensor signal invalid / drift
applicable_location: alarm_reference.pdf: Page 1, Alarm A17; ECN-1058.pdf: Section 1
notes: ECN-1058 clarifies sensor reference for A17 without altering 150 bar threshold.

question: Is PS-04 the same component as PS-04A?
expected_answer: No, PS-04 and PS-04A are distinct components and are not form-fit-function interchangeable. PS-04 was the original discharge pressure sensor that exhibited signal drift beyond tolerance after approximately 18 months. PS-04A uses an updated signal conditioning circuit to eliminate drift, requires controller firmware revision 3.2 or later, and replaced PS-04 per ECN-1042.
required_supporting_facts: PS-04 and PS-04A are NOT the same component
PS-04 experienced 18-month signal drift causing nuisance A19 alarms
PS-04A features updated signal conditioning circuit
PS-04A requires controller firmware >= 3.2
PS-04A is NOT a form-fit-function replacement
applicable_location: ECN-1042.pdf: Section 1 & Section 2; component_register.xlsx: Rows 4 & 5
notes: Negative disambiguation rule PS-04 != PS-04A enforced.

question: What action is required if alarm A17 persists for more than 10 seconds?
expected_answer: If alarm A17 persists for more than 10 seconds, the operator must execute Shutdown Procedure 4.7 before investigating further: close isolation valve IV-21, confirm hydraulic pressure decay, switch the POWER selector to OFF, tag out the system per site lockout/tagout procedure, and proceed to troubleshooting.

question: Under what circumstances must the controller not be reset?
expected_answer: The PLC-03 controller must NOT be reset while hydraulic system pressure is above 50 bar. The system must be bled below 50 bar first. Resetting the controller under pressure re-initializes valve driver outputs and can cause an uncommanded actuation/transition of isolation valve IV-21.

Resetting under pressure re-initializes valve drivers and can cause uncommanded valve movement
Pressure must be bled below 50 bar prior to reset

notes: Safety interlock enforced in both documentation and controller firmware parameter.
